content.question: How does hierarchical clustering begin, and how does it proceed?
options: It starts from K random centroids and refines them until convergence.
It starts by treating each data point as a separate cluster, then iteratively merges the closest clusters based on a chosen distance metric such as Euclidean or Manhattan.
It starts with one big cluster and splits it randomly until each point stands alone.
It starts by selecting a random point and expanding a cluster around it via a t-distribution.
content.answer: It starts by treating each data point as a separate cluster, then iteratively merges the closest clusters based on a chosen distance metric such as Euclidean or Manhattan.
